title: Rename *Byte fields to *Char to match actual UTF-16 semantics
context: Fields named startByte/endByte/atByte in helm.ts and k8sManifest.ts were computed via JS string indexing (.length, .indexOf()), which counts UTF-16 code units, not UTF-8 bytes. The misleading names created a false contract and risk of misuse. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Systematically rename all *Byte fields to *Char throughout helm.ts, k8sManifest.ts, indexer.ts, and tests to accurately reflect that these values are character offsets, not byte offsets. Map them into shared ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall arrays with explicit comments noting the semantic equivalence.
consequences: Field names now honestly reflect their actual content (UTF-16 code unit indices)
Eliminates a footgun where callers might assume byte-based math
Requires coordinated updates across multiple files and call sites
All tests updated to use new field names
alternatives_rejected: Keep misleading names and add clarifying comments only (names still lie)
Compute actual UTF-8 byte offsets (would change all values, much larger refactor)
Add a type wrapper to distinguish char vs byte offsets (unnecessary complexity for a naming issue)
